summary: Converts one indexed channel into many binary channels, or converts many binary channels back into one selected index channel.

key_params.name: fanop
key_params.note: Operation: Fan Out or Fan In

key_params.name: channame
key_params.note: Output channel names; also controls Fan Out channel count

key_params.name: range
key_params.note: How Fan Out handles values outside 0 to N-1

key_params.name: zero
key_params.note: Set all output channels to 0 for out-of-range indices

key_params.name: alloff
key_params.note: Fan In output when all input channels are off

key_params.name: set0
key_params.note: Return 0 when all channels are off

key_params.name: setneg
key_params.note: Return -1 when all channels are off

key_params.name: quantize
key_params.note: Quantize Fan Out indices to integers

key_concepts: Converts one indexed channel to many binary channels or converts many binary channels back to one selected index.
Fan Out sets exactly one output channel to 1 based on the input channel's 0-based index value.
The Channel Names parameter controls the generated Fan Out channel count.
Fan Out assumes one integer-like input channel; fractions are truncated or quantized and extra channels are ignored.
Outside Range controls whether bad Fan Out indices clamp, loop, or output all zeroes.
Fan In returns the first on channel when multiple binary inputs are on.
common_gotchas: Fan Out expects one integer-like input channel; fractions are truncated or quantized and extra input channels are ignored.
Fan Out creates one binary output per channel name.
Fan In returns the first on channel when multiple inputs are on.
Use Outside Range deliberately so bad indices do not accidentally select a boundary channel.
